correctness.rationale: The ambient algebra is exactly the countable ℓ∞-product covered by arXiv:2609.32330v1, Corollary 10.7. Invertibility in this product is coordinatewise with a uniform inverse-norm bound. The displayed finite geometric-series inverses give the closed unit disk exactly as the spectrum. The polynomial norm identity follows from von Neumann’s inequality plus finite-support approximation to the unilateral shift, and spectral mapping then gives the polynomial spectral statement. The proof handles \(\lambda=0\), \(0<|\lambda|<1\), \(|\lambda|=1\), and \(|\lambda|>1\) separately. No numerical experiment or unverified certificate is used; the main risk is only transcription of standard shift facts, which were reconstructed explicitly.

value.rationale: The result isolates a structural limitation of the newly introduced finite-detection Calkin framework: joint faithfulness and exact norm detection at finite levels do not imply fixed-stage spectral detection. The obstruction is exact rather than qualitative: every finite image is nilpotent, while globally the element has the full closed disk as essential spectrum and an isometric disk-algebra functional calculus. This is a natural boundary question for the focal realization theorem, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The limitation is that it treats one explicit canonical sequence and does not classify when spectral recovery can be restored.
